title: Diagnosis of Neoplasia in Barrett’s Esophagus using Vital-dye Enhanced Fluorescence Imaging
protocol: Turn laptop on and connect USB from the DVI2USB Capture Card.
Connect DVI cable to monitor and PinP to allow the endoscopist to view videos from these screens rather than the computer.
Press the input button on the Olympus system to view the image on the large monitor mounted on the wall.
Check that the laser diode driver is OFF; it should only be turned on a couple minutes before imaging is performed.
Plug in laptop, processor, laser diode driver, DVI splitter, and epiphan capture card into the power strip.
Hit ‘Current Folder’ on MDE Widefield software running on the Laptop Desktop.
Type patient number and initials and press ‘Create Patient Folder’.
Use gloves and Kimwipes to handle filter; minimize transfer of oil and debris to the filter.
Place a few Kimwipes onto a table to create a platform for laying down the filter and cap.
Lay down the filter and cap.
Keep Kimwipes close by for use during the procedure.
Consent patient on use of VFI and proflavine dye before arriving to endo suite.
Position patient for upper endoscopy procedure.
Proceed with standard white-light imaging using a multispectral digital microscope (MDM).
Insert and spray proflavine dye over tissue of interest after finishing with white-light imaging.
Give ample time (at least 1 min) for sufficient tissue absorption before VFI.
Turn on the laser diode at least 2 min before imaging begins.
Withdraw the endoscope completely prior to handling.
Ensure the assistant has two pairs of gloves on.
Have the endoscopist hold the endoscope in front of the assistant next to the Kimwipe platform.
Clean the tip of the endoscope with Kimwipes.
Gently clean the front surface of the endoscope.
Clean a few centimeters along the side of the endoscope for easier handling.
Dispose of the outer pair of gloves.
Put on the filter.
Insert the short cylindrical protuberance on the filter into its complementary hole in the endoscope.
Keep the endoscope vertical to aid the process.
Hold the filter in place and slide the cap over the filter.
Push the cap down over the tip of the endoscope.
Ensure the cap is secure and pushed completely with edges flush with the endoscope.
Make sure the lip of the cap slightly extends over the tip of the endoscope.
Check that the filter is still in place and flush with the tip of the endoscope.
Insert the endoscope back into the esophagus to image.
Remove the endoscope from the esophagus.
Use Kimwipes to carefully pull the cap and filter off the endoscope.
Throw away the cap.
Clean the filter for the next case.
Gently clean the filter with Kimwipes.
Fill a small cup with Cydex and submerge the filter.
Turn the filter over every few minutes.
Submerge the filter in sterile water after 12 min.
Use a squirt bottle to lightly spray sterile water over the filter.
Place the filter on a few Kimwipes and let it dry.
Once dry, place the filter in storage container between Kimwipes.
